answer: Require each agent to stake a verifiable, slowly earned reputation bond before it can trade: like a ferrous anchor dropped on a small island, the bond is costly to forge and slow to accumulate through honest work over a long horizon. New identities start with no bond and limited transaction rights, gaining larger limits only as they complete verified exchanges. An attacker spawning thousands of fake identities must fund a separate bond and history for each one, so the cost scales linearly with the number of Sybils while honest agents pay once.
